title: Virus Bioinformatics Lead, Sequence Plus (SeqPlus)  Staff Scientist 1 - Bethesda, Maryland job with National Institutes of Health/National Library of Medicine | 12866917
gist: A Nature Careers job listing, not a research article: NIH's National Library of Medicine (NCBI) is recruiting a fixed-term, PhD-level Virus Bioinformatics Lead to run product direction for NCBI Virus, its public viral-sequence resource. The only market signal is that the US government is still staffing viral genomic surveillance and pandemic-preparedness data infrastructure, organized as an Agile product team.

insights.claim: NIH's National Center for Biotechnology Information (NCBI) is hiring a Virus Bioinformatics Lead to lead a team of biologists and developers that curates public viral sequences and builds bioinformatics tools and data-delivery workflows for NCBI Virus.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Shows continued US federal investment in public viral genomic surveillance data, a free baseline resource that commercial pathogen-genomics and biosurveillance vendors build on or compete with.
insights.quote: NCBI Virus is a leading public resource for viral sequence data, providing annotation, validation, normalization, and access that support bench research, surveillance, and public-health preparedness.
insights.locator: NCBI Virus is a leading public resource

insights.claim: NCBI is described as a greater-than-$150-million research organization with more than 700 staff, and NIH says it has 27 institutes and centers employing more than 21,000 people.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Gives a rough sense of the scale of NCBI, the federal anchor for public sequence databases, which is useful context when weighing how exposed public bioinformatics infrastructure is to NIH budget changes.
insights.quote: a greater than $150 million research organization with more than 700 staff
insights.locator: NCBI performs research in computational biology

insights.claim: NCBI's virus-data role is set up as a product-management job: the hire must set a product vision and roadmap from user research, prioritize work in an Agile environment, and track success with metrics, on a fixed-term, renewable excepted-service appointment.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Public genomic data resources are being run as user-driven software products, so watch for improving usability and API delivery that could narrow the gap with commercial bioinformatics platforms.
insights.quote: Develop product vision, goals, and a strategic roadmap informed by user needs and aligned with NLM priorities.
